chapter_title: Concerning the Dragon with Fourteen Heads; what it

6.original: [and reveal its likeness and its observation above and below, it wages war by]
6.content: and reveal its likeness and its observation above and below, it wages war by

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Dragon of the Proprium

**¶1:** There exists a ruling falsity of the selfhood possessing fourteen powers of dominion, and it is gathered inward and [GAP-1] concealed within a hidden interior state furnished with five containing forms in the natural mind where it takes refuge.

**¶3:** Again, this is the manner in which the natural mind [GAP-2] pertains to this falsity, inasmuch as it is recognized as the persuasion of the proprium — a corporeal falsity ruling from self-love [GAP-3]. This ruling falsity is the very doctrine [GAP-4] of self-derived life, the intelligence of the selfhood [GAP-5]. And the fourteen powers of dominion that are distributed throughout this ruling falsity are these:

**¶4:** The seven natural faculties of perception belonging to the external mind are: the two of intellectual apprehension, by which one discerns; the two of obedience and reception, by which one perceives what is communicated; the two of interior discernment, by which one detects what is spiritually agreeable or repugnant; also the faculty of discrimination [GAP-6], by which one selects, receiving there the various qualities of delight and aversion that arise in every form of experience.

**¶5:** These are the seven powers of the ruling falsity — the seven faculties of natural perception that belong to the interior rational degree of the person; [GAP-7] and corresponding to these are seven belonging to the exterior sensual degree below. The seven of the exterior natural mind are these: two [GAP-8]; the two [GAP-9] governing faculty [GAP-10] — corresponding to the seven powers of dominion that operate interiorly above; so together with the ones that operate in the sensual degree below, they complete and constitute fourteen powers of dominion belonging to the ruling falsity of the selfhood.

**¶6:** Conversely, the five hidden recesses of which it has been taught, where the ruling falsity is concentrated and from which it extends itself, are these: the first is the faculty of outward expression and communication; the second is the faculty of spiritual thought and interior respiration; the third is the will, the seat of love; the fourth is the faculty that mediates the purification or corruption of affections; the fifth is the living truth — or its profanation — that flows through all of them. Again, if this falsity should project itself outward from these interior recesses, [GAP-11: REVIEW — and manifest its character and exercise its perception both into the interior rational and exterior sensual degrees, it wages spiritual combat through] its fourteen powers of dominion.

**¶7:** — this ruling falsity, which is the self-derived thinking of the proprium.

**¶8:** — the ruling falsity that exists with its fourteen powers of dominion and five concealed interior states, within which it is hidden and harbored. It accomplishes through these recesses [GAP-12: its contin­ual] craving and self-will at every moment.

---

*Note on the overall structure:* The teaching describes the complete anatomy of self-derived intelligence — the proprium's own "doctrine of the flesh." The fourteen heads are not mere natural organs but the full set of cognitive and sensory faculties through which the selfhood exercises dominion over the whole person, interior and exterior alike. The five dens represent the deepest containing forms of the natural mind — expression, thought, will, affective mediation, and the vital medium that connects them all — within which evil love conceals itself and from which it wages its war against regeneration.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: there is a dragon with fourteen heads, and it is gathered in and [hidden in its] den with five refuges.

Again, this is how this earth [is likened] to it, as it is accounted a corporeal dragon [of desire] the dragon is this doctrine [and teaching] of the flesh [and its thought] also the fourteen heads that are distributed over the dragon are these.

The seven sense organs on the head of the body are the two of sight by which one sees; the two of sound by which one hears; the two of scent by which one smells; also the tongue [of taste] by which one selects, receiving there the different tastes that occur in every form.

These are the seven heads of the dragon, the seven sense organs that are on the upper part of the person; [and seven are] below. The seven of the torso are these: two [hands]; the two [feet] ruler [they correspond to] the seven heads that are above; so with the ones below they total and make fourteen heads of the dragon.

Conversely, the five dens about which they have spoken, where the dragon is congregated and protrudes, are these: the first is the tongue; the second is the lungs; the third is the heart; the fourth is the spleen; the fifth is the blood that dwells in them. Again, if it shall look out from them [and reveal its likeness and its observation above and below, it wages war by] its fourteen heads.
the dragon, which is the thought of the body
the dragon that exists with its fourteen heads and five dens, wherein it is concealed and hidden. It does through them [all its evil deeds, fulfilling its will and its des]ire all the time.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "concealed within a hidden interior state," and the natural text requires a phrase connecting "gathered in and" to "den with five refuges," yielding "gathered in and hidden in its den."

The spiritual reading says "the natural mind pertains to this falsity," and the passage explains how the earth is compared to the dragon; "is likened" provides the needed comparison verb before "to it."

The spiritual reading specifies "ruling from self-love" at this position; in the Manichaean register of the Kephalaia, amor sui (self-love) is rendered as "desire" (ἐπιθυμία), yielding "a corporeal dragon of desire."

The spiritual reading says "the very doctrine of self-derived life," and the Kephalaia commonly uses doubled expressions; "doctrine and teaching of the flesh" is a standard Coptic doublet reinforcing the concept.

The spiritual reading says "the intelligence of the selfhood," and ¶7 explicitly identifies the dragon as "the thought of the body"; "of the flesh and its thought" directly mirrors this identification.

The established pattern is "the two of sight," "the two of sound," "the two of scent," so the tongue follows as "of taste"; confirmed by the spiritual reading's "faculty of discrimination" and the text's own "receiving there the different tastes."

The spiritual reading says "corresponding to these are seven belonging to the exterior sensual degree below," and the text needs a transition from the upper seven to introduce the lower seven before the word "below."

The lower seven are the active counterparts to the upper perceptive organs; hands are the primary instruments of outward action in the body's torso/limb region, corresponding to the eyes as instruments of perception above.
Feet are the second major paired members of the lower body, commonly listed alongside hands in Manichaean body enumerations as instruments of the will's outward movement.
The spiritual reading says "corresponding to the seven powers of dominion that operate interiorly above," requiring a comparative phrase linking the lower set to the upper seven heads.

fills.explanation: The editor's fill maps precisely to the spiritual reading: "reveal its likeness" = "manifest its character," "its observation" = "exercise its perception," "above and below" = interior and exterior degrees, "wages war by" = wages spiritual combat through — all confirmed.

fills.fill: all its evil deeds, fulfilling its will and its des
fills.explanation: The spiritual reading says "its continual craving and self-will"; the dragon accomplishes evil works through the five dens, fulfilling both its will (self-will) and its desire (craving), with the fill ending in "its des" to form "its desire" with the surviving text.
